label: PERMISSION_2: issued strong authorization
definition: Strong n p means n.issued p. Norms supplies an extensional family of outcome predicates as a primitive issued-content input. No issuance history, legitimate authority, closure, feasibility or ideal compatibility is implicit.
note: Analyst semantics for #1398. Interpretation and legitimate normative authority remain OPEN. See docs/notes/carneades-deontology-boundary.md, Ross section.

formal_gap.meaning: RossPermission.Strong n p says that the authorization with content p has been issued: p belongs to the norm source's issued contents. Its body is n.issued p, so its content is that supplied membership. Norms n is a supplied extensional family of outcome predicates (n.issued) in TruthCore.Ethics.RossPermission (#1398).
examples: In the Ross test model, an authorization issued with the content 'mail the letter'.
exclusions: Permission as compatibility with the ideal (the weak, ideal-compatible permission sense; disambiguation 7a45ad77).
Any issuance history, legitimate authority, closure under entailment or feasibility: none is implicit.
open_obligations: The interpretation and the legitimacy of the normative authority remain OPEN (docs/notes/carneades-deontology-boundary.md, Ross section).
No formalization candidate: issued content is a supplied input.
